nws.synopsis: Calm and warmer weather will occur through Wednesday. The warmest days of the week will be today and Monday with marine layer clouds returning by Tuesday or Wednesday morning near the coast. Cooler and breezier with increased chances for precipitation entering the picture by later in the week.
systems: As pressure heights subtly lower, this will increase the depth of the marine layer.
Low clouds and patchy fog may form offshore and near coastal areas as early as Tuesday morning, with higher confidence on this occurring by Tuesday night into Wednesday morning.
Like yesterday, models continue to show an area of low pressure entering the Pacific Northwest around Wednesday into Thursday, where a large troughing pattern begins to set up across the West Coast.
This will bring a deeper marine layer and a cooling trend to the region starting Thursday into next weekend.

sites.name: Little Black
sites.note: Best post-frontal site in the county. West-facing, so offshore mornings are over the back.

sites.name: Blossom Valley
sites.note: Inland thermal site; often lines up with Elsinore.

sites.name: Elsinore (E / Edwards)
sites.note: East-facing over the lake; its own animal. The sea-breeze convergence line is the XC engine.

sites.name: Torrey Pines
sites.note: Ridge soaring in a steady W to WNW sea breeze. SW or NW is cross (soarable but not great); only east is over the back. Rare thermal days (1,200 ft+) are flagged as a Thermal day.

sites.name: Laguna / Horse
sites.note: Two launches: Horse faces west, Laguna faces east over the desert. Each is scored on its own and the better one is shown.

sites.name: Otay Mesa
sites.note: Near the border; XC goes north and east.

sites.name: Soboba
sites.note: Flight park on the San Jacinto front.

sites.name: Santa Barbara (Skyport)
sites.note: South-facing front range above Santa Barbara; launch sits above the marine layer, so thermals are measured from the slopes at launch height. Sundowners and other real north winds are over the back.
